question.text: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the order in which the principal constitutional and contractual documents of a trust-form AIF are typically put in place?

answer.text: Investment Management Agreement > Trust Deed > PPM > Contribution Agreement
Trust Deed (constitutional document) > Investment Management Agreement > Contribution Agreement > PPM
PPM > Trust Deed > Investment Management Agreement > Contribution Agreement
Contribution Agreement > PPM > Investment Management Agreement > Trust Deed

explanation.text: The Logic: XIX-D pp. 179-183 describes the Trust Deed as the constitutional document that creates the fund and appoints the trustee. The trustee then enters into the Investment Management Agreement (IMA) with the investment manager. The investor relationship documents (such as the Contribution Agreement with each contributor) sit alongside the PPM, which is the offer/disclosure document, and other service agreements follow. The Trap: The other options either invert the creation order or place a disclosure/offer document above the constitutional and management contracts that authorise the AIF in the first place. Note: The pages checked do not state a strict precedence hierarchy placing the PPM above the Contribution Agreement, nor do they support a side-letter override or manager-discretion override mechanism. The question and explanation use only the source's principal-document ordering: constitutional document/Trust Deed, IMA, Contribution Agreement and PPM, then service agreements.
